[031]
There are three useful measurements: synthesis time, generated audio duration, and playback runway. Together they reveal whether the generator is keeping ahead of the device, whether chunks are too ambitious, and whether a pause came from document structure or starvation.

[032]
The migration has one hard requirement: existing keyboard shortcuts must continue working. It also has two softer goals: reduce native packaging complexity, and make failures visible in ordinary logs without requiring a debugger.
---
[033]
The cache contains immutable facts about the text: sentence marks, clause marks, commas, and their absolute offsets. The controller contributes one changing value: the target length derived from current playback runway.
---
[034]
The release checklist is straightforward: build both native targets, run the Python suite, launch from the installed entry point, and verify a real capture. If all four steps pass, the artifact is ready for a longer listening test.
---
[035]
The debug panel uses a compact sequence: captured, prepared, chunk ready, chunk playing, and completed. Each event carries only the fields it owns, which keeps producers independent and makes missing transitions immediately obvious.
---
[036]
The fallback order is intentional: prefer punctuation nearest the requested size, accept the end of the current structural line, and use whitespace only when the safe window contains no usable punctuation. A hard character cut is the final emergency case.
---
[037]
For OCR capture, the states are equally small: idle, waiting for selection, waiting for clipboard, and finished. Cancellation can return any active state to idle, while an unrelated clipboard update simply keeps the wait active.
---
[038]
The configuration stores seconds as floating-point values: a short structural pause, a clipboard timeout, and an optional startup delay. Validation rejects negative values, because silently converting them would hide a typing error.
---
[039]
The native adapter exports four operations: create, speak, cancel, and destroy. Python wraps those calls in one object, translates native failures into ordinary exceptions, and ensures destruction happens exactly once even during shutdown.
---
[040]
One principle guides the package layout: modules that change for the same reason should live together. Input capture belongs under input, speech generation belongs under speech, and window or tray behavior belongs under the user-interface package.
---
[041]

[061]
The first synthesis request should remain compact, because playback cannot begin until it finishes, but compact does not mean arbitrary: a colon near the target provides a coherent setup, followed by a larger explanation that can be generated while earlier audio is already playing.

[062]

[063]

[064]
A healthy queue permits a larger request, while an almost empty queue calls for less work, yet neither condition changes the grammar already present in the text: commas, colons, sentence endings, and line boundaries remain available under every timing state.

[068]

[069]
When the safe window contains several choices, distance to the live target is the only ranking rule: a punctuation mark just before the target can beat one farther after it, and a nearby colon can beat a remote sentence ending without special-case flags.
---
[070]
Whitespace is not grammar, so it should never win merely because buffer runway is comfortable or a comma flag happens to be disabled; it becomes eligible only when no usable punctuation exists inside the fixed window: this keeps audible phrasing consistent.

[085]

- Confirm the tray icon appears

- Press Alt+D for OCR capture
- Inspect chunk boundaries in the debug panel
- Exit and confirm native hooks are released
---
[086]
### Architecture
Input capture converts external events into prepared text.
Speech planning converts prepared text into bounded segments.
Backends convert segments into audio frames.
Playback converts queued frames into sound and word highlights.
---
[087]
Diagnostics
capture.source: clipboard
speech.backend: natural
chunk.target: 100
chunk.actual: 97
playback.runway: 4.8 seconds
completion.status: drained
The structured fields should remain understandable when read as prose.
---
[088]
Checklist:
- Text is preserved from start to finish
- The first prose chunk is not a tiny acknowledgement
- No chunk exceeds two hundred characters
- Non-final chunks prefer punctuation
- Whitespace is used only as a bounded fallback
---
[089]
## Troubleshooting
If the shortcut does not respond, verify that the native input DLL exists.
If OCR returns nothing, check whether the clipboard sequence changed.
If playback pauses, compare synthesis duration with buffered runway.
If launch fails, inspect runtime path resolution.

An OCR artifact inserted the replacement character � beside one word, embedded an object marker ￼ beside another, and split a sentence across irregular spacing. Preparation removes the markers, collapses excess whitespace, and keeps the remaining characters in order.

[095]
The quotation ended with punctuation.” The next sentence began normally, although OCR had converted one apostrophe into a curly mark. Boundary detection must include the closing quote so the following chunk never starts with a stranded quotation character.

[096]
Mixed language text can include español, français, Deutsch, and 日本語 in the same selection. The chunker counts Python characters rather than encoded bytes, so nearby punctuation remains stable and no multibyte character is cut in half.

[097]
The source used dashes — like this — instead of commas for several asides, then finally reached a colon: because dashes are not cached boundaries, the colon should win if it lies inside the safety window; otherwise whitespace is the bounded fallback.
---
[098]
OCR sometimes reads “1” as “l”, merges rn into m, or inserts | between nearby columns. Those recognition errors belong to the OCR layer, not chunk selection; the speech pipeline must preserve the received text and choose boundaries without attempting speculative correction.

[100]
This last block restates the contract in plain language: prepare the selection once, index its punctuation once, calculate each desired size from live playback runway, choose the closest cached boundary inside two hundred characters, and use whitespace only when no usable mark is available.
